messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Suppressing unneeded \begin{kframe}..\end{kframe} and how to suppress ##
parts:
For the first question, you can reset the chunk hook:

knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) x) # do not wrap output in kframe

For the second, you may use the chunk option comment=NA
(http://yihui.name/knitr/options)

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Suppressing unneeded \begin{kframe}..\end{kframe} and how to suppress ##
parts:
Frank, I think you can set any chunk options to global SweaveOpts, i.e. put this line in your latex preamble.

% \SweaveOpts(comment=NA)

Note that it's read by knitr despite being commented out in latex I believe?  Yihui can correct me if I'm wrong about this.

Wonderful.  Thanks Yihui.  On the second part is there a way to make
the comment=NA a global option so I only need to specify it once?

Frank Harrell

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Suppressing unneeded \begin{kframe}..\end{kframe} and how to suppress ##
parts:
Yes, any options can be set globally via \SweaveOpts{}. Or if you want
it to be even more "global", you can change the default setting of
knitr permanently by opts_chunk$set(comment = NA) before you start to
knit() any documents.

BTW, I have been thinking of putting together a set of hook functions
for listings in knitr so that you only need to call something like
render_listings() to get listings output. I do not use listings very
often by myself, but I believe there must be a number of people
interested in this. I know you have been working on it, so I will be
happy to wrap up your listings hooks (including the LaTeX preamble
settings) into knitr in the next version if you like. Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui

parts:
Wonderful.  Thanks Yihui.  On the second part is there a way to make
the comment=NA a global option so I only need to specify it once?

Also, R raw output appears in an italic font that is variable width.
When the output represents multiple rows of a long vector, the columns
to not line up. I define Routstyle as follows, for the listings
package.

\lstdefinestyle{Routstyle}{fancyvrb=false,literate={~}{{$\sim$}}1{R^2}
{{$R^{2}$}}2{^}{{$^{\scriptstyle\wedge}$}}1{R-squared}{{$R^{2}$}}2,%
frame=single,framerule=0.2pt,framesep=1pt,basicstyle=\Routcolor
\Routsize,%
backgroundcolor=\Routbackground}

How do I get knitr to put R output in a fixed width font? Maybe
Routstyle needs a \texttt somewhere.

Frank Harrell

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Suppressing unneeded \begin{kframe}..\end{kframe} and how to suppress ##
parts:
Frank,

One option: I use this in my .rnw file to wrap the output in an Soutput environment, which I already had defined from Sweave days to use a fixed-width font.

<<setup, echo=FALSE,results=hide>>=
knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  paste('\\begin{Soutput}\n', x, '\\end{Soutput}\n', sep = '')
})
@

Kevin
